records.issue_text: Query fetching previous check-ins is unbounded at the DB level; full check-in history is loaded into memory and only sliced in Python instead of limiting the queryset
records.rationale: The queryset is sliced before evaluation, which applies a DB-level LIMIT in Django. In `try_incident_threshold`, after building the queryset with `.filter(...).order_by("-date_added").values(...)`, it does `previous_checkins = list(reversed(previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]))`, where `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` is a queryset slice (SQL LIMIT), not a Python slice of an already-materialized full history. So the diff contradicts the claim that the full check-in history is loaded into memory.
records.stripped_text: Query fetching previous check-ins is unbounded at the DB level; full check-in history is loaded into memory and only sliced in Python instead of limiting the queryset

records.issue_text: get_failure_reason produces degenerate output (' check-ins detected') when all failed check-ins have statuses outside HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP
records.rationale: In `get_failure_reason`, `status_counts` only includes check-ins whose `status` is in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`. If none match, `status_counts` is empty, so the list passed to `get_text_list([...])` is empty. `human_status` will then be an empty string, and the function returns `_("%(problem_checkins)s check-ins detected") % {"problem_checkins": human_status}`, yielding a degenerate string like `" check-ins detected"`.
records.stripped_text: get_failure_reason produces degenerate output (' check-ins detected') when all failed check-ins have statuses outside HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP

Under Django autocommit, if `get_or_create` raises (DB error, constraint, etc.), the status change would remain committed while no incident row exists, matching the described partial-failure state.
